enhanced_information: Virgin T lymphocytes use L-selectin and CCR7 to extravasate to the lymph node. L-selectin facilitates the initial tethering and rolling of T lymphocytes on high endothelial venules (HEVs) in the lymph nodes. CCR7 is crucial for responding to chemokines CCL19 and CCL21, which are present in the lymph node environment, guiding the T cells through chemotaxis towards the lymph node. The retrieved evidence supports the interaction of L-selectin with endothelial cells, which is a key step in the extravasation process. The chemokine interaction evidence, while broad, aligns with the role of CCR7 in chemotaxis. Therefore, the correct pair of surface molecules used by virgin T lymphocytes for extravasation to the lymph node is CCR7 and L-selectin, as reflected in option 'opa'.
analysis: Virgin T lymphocytes, also known as naive T cells, use specific surface molecules to extravasate into lymph nodes. The key molecules involved in this process are CCR7 and L-selectin. CCR7 is a chemokine receptor that guides T cells to lymph nodes by responding to chemokines CCL19 and CCL21, which are present in high concentrations in lymphoid tissues. L-selectin (CD62L) is an adhesion molecule that facilitates the initial tethering and rolling of T cells on high endothelial venules (HEVs) in lymph nodes. This combination of CCR7 and L-selectin is well-documented in immunology as the mechanism for naive T cell homing to lymph nodes.
